topics.title: Direction cosines and direction ratios of a line

learn.hook: A drone climbs from a rooftop in Bengaluru towards a tower. Three numbers, its direction cosines, pin down that heading in 3D space.
points: Vector algebra lets us describe lines in space neatly. If a line makes angles α, β, γ with the x-, y-, z-axes, its direction cosines are l = cos α, m = cos β, n = cos γ.
Direction ratios a, b, c are any numbers proportional to l, m, n. A line has infinitely many sets of direction ratios.
From direction ratios: l = a/√(a² + b² + c²), m = b/√(…), n = c/√(…) (or all with the opposite sign).
Line through P(x₁, y₁, z₁) and Q(x₂, y₂, z₂): direction ratios x₂ − x₁, y₂ − y₁, z₂ − z₁; divide by PQ for direction cosines.
Three points are collinear if the direction ratios of AB and BC are proportional. (The derivation of l² + m² + n² = 1 is not in the current syllabus; the result is used.)

example.q: Find the direction cosines of the line through P(−2, 4, −5) and Q(1, 2, 3).

learn.reallife: If GPS gives the coordinates of a base camp and of a ledge above it, the differences of the coordinates are direction ratios of the straight rope line between them; any proportional set describes the same line.

items.q: l² + m² + n² for any line

games.title: Direction facts
items: A line has exactly one set of direction ratios.
2, 4, 6 and 1, 2, 3 are direction ratios of the same line.
The direction cosines of the y-axis are 0, 1, 0.
It makes angles 90°, 0°, 90° with the axes.
Points A(2, 3, 4), B(−1, −2, 1), C(5, 8, 7) are collinear.
AB has ratios −3, −5, −3 and BC has 6, 10, 6, which are proportional.
If l = m = n, then l = 1/3.

The sum of the coordinates of each point is odd

steps: Proportional ratios with the common point B ⇒ collinear
Answer: Direction ratios of AB (−3, −5, −3) and BC (6, 10, 6) are proportional
quiz.mistake: Uses equal lengths as the test

quiz.q: If a line has direction cosines l, m, n with l = 1/3 and m = 2/3, what is n² ?

quiz.explain: l = m = n and 3l² = 1 gives l = 1/√3.

quiz.q:
Assertion (A): −2, 1, 2 can be direction ratios of the line with direction cosines 2/3, −1/3, −2/3.
Reason (R): Direction ratios may be any non-zero multiple of the direction cosines, including a negative multiple.
options: Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true and R explains A
A is false but R is true
quiz.explain: −2, 1, 2 = −3 × (2/3, −1/3, −2/3), so they are proportional. R explains A.
steps: R: direction ratios can be any non-zero multiple, even negative — true
R is the reason A holds
Answer: Both A and R are true and R explains A
quiz.mistake: Thinks a negative multiple gives a different line

teach.praise: Tweet! Direction cosines are cosines of the angles with the axes, squares adding to 1; ratios are any proportional set!
teach.nudge: How do you turn direction ratios into direction cosines?

revise.summary: A line's direction cosines are the cosines of its angles with the axes, and direction ratios are any numbers proportional to them. For the line through two points, the direction ratios are the coordinate differences.
focus: Convert direction ratios to direction cosines
Find direction ratios of the line through two points
remember: l = a/√(a² + b² + c²), and similarly m, n
Through P, Q: DRs x₂ − x₁, y₂ − y₁, z₂ − z₁
traps: Divide by √(a² + b² + c²), not by a² + b² + c²
A negative multiple of the DRs is still the same line

topics.title: Equation of a line in space

learn.hook: One point and one direction: that is all you need to describe a straight line in space, whether it is a laser beam or a metro tunnel.
points: Vector form: a line through the point with position vector a, parallel to b, is r = a + λb (λ a real parameter).
Cartesian form: through (x₁, y₁, z₁) with direction ratios a, b, c: (x − x₁)/a = (y − y₁)/b = (z − z₁)/c.
To convert Cartesian to vector: read the point (x₁, y₁, z₁) and the direction (a, b, c) from the denominators.
A line parallel to a given line has the same direction ratios.
Watch signs: (x + 3)/2 means x₁ = −3. Write the form as x − x₁ before reading off the point.

example.q: Find the vector and Cartesian equations of the line through (5, 2, −4) parallel to 3i + 2j − 8k.

learn.reallife: A laser beam, or the centre line of a straight tunnel, is fixed by one starting point and one direction; every point on it fits r = a + λb.

quiz.q: Which is the vector equation of the line through (1, 2, 3) parallel to 3i + 2j − 2k?
quiz.explain: r = a + λb with a the point and b the direction.
steps: Vector form: r = a + λb, a = point, b = direction
quiz.mistake: Swaps the point and the direction

quiz.q: What point does the line (x + 3)/2 = (y − 5)/4 = (z + 6)/2 pass through?
quiz.explain: x + 3 = x − (−3), so x₁ = −3; similarly y₁ = 5 and z₁ = −6.
quiz.mistake: Reads the signs directly without rewriting

quiz.q: Which is the Cartesian equation of the line through the origin and (5, −2, 3)?
quiz.mistake: Writes the coordinates as multipliers instead of denominators

quiz.q: Which line is parallel to (x − 1)/2 = (y + 3)/(−1) = z/4?
steps: Parallel line needs proportional direction: 4i − 2j + 8k = 2(2i − j + 4k) ✓
quiz.mistake: Compares points instead of directions

quiz.q: Write the vector equation of the line (x − 5)/3 = (y + 4)/7 = (z − 6)/2. What is its direction vector?
steps: In (x − x₁)/a = (y − y₁)/b = (z − z₁)/c, the denominators a, b, c give the direction
quiz.mistake: Uses the point as the direction

quiz.q: The line through A(3, 4, −7) and B(1, −1, 6) has which vector equation?
quiz.mistake: Uses the second point as the direction

quiz.q: Which point lies on the line r = i + 2j − k + λ(2i − j + k)?
quiz.mistake: Takes the direction vector as a point on the line

quiz.q:
Assertion (A): (x − 2)/3 = (y − 1)/0 = (z + 1)/4 represents a line with y = 1 for every point.
Reason (R): A zero denominator means that coordinate stays fixed along the line.
options: Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R explains A
quiz.explain: Direction ratio 0 for y means the line never moves in the y direction, so y = 1 throughout.
steps: R: a zero direction ratio means that coordinate does not change along the line — true
Here the y direction ratio is 0, so y stays at y₁ = 1
So A is true because of R
Answer: Both A and R are true and R explains A
quiz.mistake: Thinks a zero denominator makes the equation meaningless

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'How do I write the equation of a line in 3D space?'
teach.praise: Chirp! Pick a point a and a direction b: r = a + λb. In Cartesian form, (x − x₁)/a = (y − y₁)/b = (z − z₁)/c!
teach.nudge: What two ingredients define a line?

revise.summary: A line through point a parallel to b is r = a + λb, or in Cartesian form (x − x₁)/a = (y − y₁)/b = (z − z₁)/c. The denominators give the direction.
focus: Write vector and Cartesian equations of a line
Read the point and direction from a given equation
Find lines through two points or parallel to a line
remember: Parallel lines have proportional direction ratios
traps: Rewrite (x + 3) as x − (−3) before reading the point
Don't swap the point and the direction
A zero denominator means that coordinate stays fixed

learn.hook: Two runways at an airport cross at an angle. Find it from their direction vectors, with no protractor needed.
points: If lines have direction ratios a₁, b₁, c₁ and a₂, b₂, c₂, the acute angle θ between them satisfies cos θ = |a₁a₂ + b₁b₂ + c₁c₂| / (√(a₁² + b₁² + c₁²) √(a₂² + b₂² + c₂²)).
In vector form: cos θ = |b₁ · b₂| / (|b₁||b₂|).
Perpendicular lines: a₁a₂ + b₁b₂ + c₁c₂ = 0.
Parallel lines: a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂.
With direction cosines, cos θ = |l₁l₂ + m₁m₂ + n₁n₂|.

example.q: Find the angle between r = 3i + 2j − 4k + λ(i + 2j + 2k) and r = 5i − 2j + μ(3i + 2j + 6k).

learn.reallife: Engineers designing a cable-stayed bridge can find the angle between two cables in 3D from their direction vectors, using exactly this formula.

quiz.q: Find cos θ for the angle between the lines with direction ratios 2, 2, 1 and 4, 1, 8.
quiz.mistake: Uses 81 instead of 3 × 9 in the denominator

quiz.q: For what value of k are lines with direction ratios 1, k, 2 and 3, −1, 2 perpendicular?
quiz.mistake: Makes a sign slip
Forgets to simplify √300 or uses the points instead of directions

quiz.q: Which pair of lines is parallel?
steps: The other pairs are not proportional (e.g. 1/3 ≠ 2/2)
quiz.mistake: Thinks a negative multiple is not parallel

quiz.q: For the lines (x − 1)/(−3) = (y − 2)/(2p/7) = (z − 3)/2 and (x − 1)/(−3p/7) = (y − 5)/1 = (z − 6)/(−5), what value of p makes them perpendicular?
quiz.mistake: Drops the sign of one of the products

quiz.q: What is the angle between lines with direction ratios 1, 1, 0 and 0, 1, 1?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to divide by the magnitudes

quiz.q: Why is the modulus used in cos θ = |b₁ · b₂|/(|b₁||b₂|)?
options: Because dot products are always positive
To get the acute angle between the lines
quiz.explain: Two lines form two supplementary angles; the modulus picks the acute one.
steps: Two crossing lines make two angles, θ and π − θ
The modulus makes cos θ ≥ 0, so θ is the acute one
Answer: To get the acute angle between the lines
quiz.mistake: Thinks the dot product cannot be negative

quiz.q:
Assertion (A): Lines with direction ratios 2, −3, 4 and 1, 2, 1 are perpendicular.
Reason (R): Two lines are perpendicular when a₁a₂ + b₁b₂ + c₁c₂ = 0.
options: Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R explains A
quiz.explain: 2 − 6 + 4 = 0, so by R the lines are perpendicular.
steps: R: perpendicular ⇔ a₁a₂ + b₁b₂ + c₁c₂ = 0 — true
So the lines are perpendicular by R
Answer: Both A and R are true and R explains A
quiz.mistake: Adds the ratios instead of multiplying

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'How do I find the angle between two lines in space?'
teach.praise: Tweet! Use the directions: cos θ = |dot product|/(product of lengths). Zero means perpendicular, proportional means parallel!
teach.nudge: What is the condition for the lines to be perpendicular?

revise.summary: The acute angle between two lines is given by cos θ = |b₁ · b₂|/(|b₁||b₂|). Lines are perpendicular when a₁a₂ + b₁b₂ + c₁c₂ = 0 and parallel when their direction ratios are proportional.
focus: Find the angle between two lines
Find an unknown for perpendicular lines
remember: cos θ = |a₁a₂ + b₁b₂ + c₁c₂| / (√(a₁² + b₁² + c₁²)√(a₂² + b₂² + c₂²))
traps: Multiply the magnitudes, don't multiply the squares
Keep the modulus for the acute angle

learn.hook: Two flyovers cross at different heights without meeting. How close do they get? That gap is the shortest distance between skew lines.
points: Skew lines are lines in space that are neither parallel nor intersecting (they lie in different planes).
The shortest distance is along the segment perpendicular to both lines.
For r = a₁ + λb₁ and r = a₂ + μb₂: d = |(a₂ − a₁) · (b₁ × b₂)| / |b₁ × b₂|.
Cartesian form: d = |det[[x₂ − x₁, y₂ − y₁, z₂ − z₁], [a₁, b₁, c₁], [a₂, b₂, c₂]]| / √[(b₁c₂ − b₂c₁)² + (c₁a₂ − c₂a₁)² + (a₁b₂ − a₂b₁)²].
If d = 0, the lines intersect.

example.q: Find the shortest distance between r = i + 2j + k + λ(i − j + k) and r = 2i − j − k + μ(2i + j + 2k).

learn.reallife: Air traffic controllers check the closest approach of two straight flight paths that do not meet; if the shortest distance is below the safety limit, one plane is moved to a different path.

games.title: Shortest distance between skew lines
items: Compute b₁ × b₂ and its magnitude
Divide the absolute value by |b₁ × b₂|

games.title: Skew line facts
items: Skew lines can exist in a plane.
Two lines in one plane are parallel or intersect.
If the shortest distance is 0, the lines intersect.
The shortest distance segment is perpendicular to both lines.
That is why b₁ × b₂ appears.
Skew lines are neither parallel nor intersecting.
The x-axis and the line through (0, 0, 5) parallel to the y-axis are skew.
They never meet and are not parallel; their distance is 5.

quiz.q: What is the shortest distance between r = i + 2j + k + λ(i − j + k) and r = 2i − j − k + μ(2i + j + 2k)?
steps: a₂ − a₁ = i − 3j − 2k; b₁ × b₂ = −3i + 0j + 3k, |b₁ × b₂| = 3√2
quiz.mistake: Forgets to divide by |b₁ × b₂|

quiz.q: What is the shortest distance between the x-axis (r = λi) and the line r = 5k + μj?
quiz.explain: a₂ − a₁ = 5k and b₁ × b₂ = i × j = k. d = |5k · k|/|k| = 5.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the lines intersect

quiz.q: Two lines have shortest distance 0. They are
quiz.explain: Zero distance means a common point.
steps: Shortest distance 0 means the lines have a common point
Lines with a common point intersect (parallel distinct lines have d > 0)

quiz.q: In d = |(a₂ − a₁) · (b₁ × b₂)|/|b₁ × b₂|, why do we use b₁ × b₂?
options: It gives the angle between the lines
It is the point of intersection
It is perpendicular to both lines, the direction of the shortest segment
It makes the answer an integer
quiz.explain: The shortest segment is perpendicular to both lines; b₁ × b₂ has exactly that direction.
steps: The shortest segment is perpendicular to both lines
b₁ × b₂ is perpendicular to both b₁ and b₂
Projecting a₂ − a₁ on it gives the shortest distance
Answer: It is perpendicular to both lines, the direction of the shortest segment
quiz.mistake: Confuses the cross product with the dot product

quiz.q: For the lines in the worked example, what is (a₂ − a₁) · (b₁ × b₂)?
quiz.mistake: Drops a negative sign

quiz.q: Find the shortest distance between (x + 1)/7 = (y + 1)/(−6) = (z + 1)/1 and (x − 3)/1 = (y − 5)/(−2) = (z − 7)/1.

quiz.q: Which pair of lines are skew?
options: r = λi and r = μi + j
r = λ(i + j) and r = μ(2i + 2j)
r = λi and r = k + μj
quiz.explain: λi and k + μj never meet (the second has z = 1) and are not parallel.
steps: λi and μi + j: same direction i ⇒ parallel ✗
λi and μj meet at the origin ✗; λ(i + j) and μ(2i + 2j) are the same line ✗
λi has z = 0, k + μj has z = 1: never meet; directions i and j are not parallel ✓
Answer: r = λi and r = k + μj
quiz.mistake: Picks parallel or intersecting lines

quiz.q:
Assertion (A): The lines r = λ(i + j + k) and r = μ(i − j) intersect.
Reason (R): Both lines pass through the origin.
options: Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true and R explains A
A is false but R is true
quiz.explain: At λ = μ = 0 both give the origin, so they meet there and their shortest distance is 0.
steps: R: λ = 0 and μ = 0 both give the origin — true
So the lines share a point: they intersect (shortest distance 0)
R is the reason A holds
Answer: Both A and R are true and R explains A
quiz.mistake: Computes a formula without noticing the common point

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'Two lines in space never meet. How do I find how close they get?'
teach.praise: Chirp! Dot the gap a₂ − a₁ with b₁ × b₂, take the absolute value, and divide by |b₁ × b₂|. Closest approach found!
teach.nudge: Which vector is perpendicular to both lines?

revise.summary: Skew lines are neither parallel nor intersecting. Their shortest distance is d = |(a₂ − a₁) · (b₁ × b₂)|/|b₁ × b₂|, and d = 0 means the lines intersect.

Decide if two lines are skew or intersecting

Take the absolute value of the dot product
Watch signs in the cross product

topics.title: Parallel lines and perpendicular lines through a point

learn.hook: Two parallel railway tracks never meet, but the gap between them matters. For parallel lines, a simpler distance formula takes over.
points: Parallel lines r = a₁ + λb and r = a₂ + μb: distance d = |b × (a₂ − a₁)| / |b|.
The skew-line formula fails here because b × b = 0.
A line perpendicular to two given lines has direction b₁ × b₂.
Line through a point a perpendicular to both b₁ and b₂: r = a + λ(b₁ × b₂).
Planes, coplanarity of lines, angle between planes and line–plane problems are not in the current CBSE syllabus.

example.q: Find the distance between r = i + 2j − 4k + λ(2i + 3j + 6k) and r = 3i + 3j − 5k + μ(2i + 3j + 6k).

learn.reallife: Indian broad-gauge rails are kept 1676 mm apart. Modelling two straight rails as parallel lines in space, the formula above gives the gap between them.

Because b₁ × b₂ = 0, making the denominator zero

Then b₁ × b₂ = 0, so |b₁ × b₂| = 0 in the denominator
